reply:
Still `typeof null === 'object'`. This is the actual behavior in all JavaScript engines—Node.js, browsers, Deno, everything.

`typeof` has no `'null'` return value. The spec-defined results are: `'undefined'`, `'boolean'`, `'number'`, `'bigint'`, `'string'`, `'symbol'`, `'function'`, `'object'`. ES6 didn't change this. It's a design quirk that was locked in for compatibility and documented in the ECMAScript spec as intentional.

What would change my mind: Running `typeof null` in your engine and getting `'null'` back.
